scores.claim_text: QCi has three granted United States patents (excluding LSI portfolio).
scores.M_value: QCI: 3 granted (11436519, 12008436, 12493811); QPhoton: 0 granted. Granted patents match the three listed in 10-K (machine-learning mapping x2 + variational analog quantum oracle learning).
scores.interpretation: Mode A exact match: 3 = 3 granted. Mode B reveals QPhoton itself holds no granted USPTO patents under that assignee name — the QPhoton tech IP appears to live via the Stevens Institute license, not native QPhoton issuances. Net: claim PASS. Note caveat below per heuristic 8: total of only 3 native granted patents is thin for a 'quantum-computing company' but matches what they disclosed.

PASS via entity resolution. Mode B was load-bearing here.

scores.claim_text: Acquired LSI on Feb 2 2026 for $110M as stalking-horse 363 bidder; aggregate rollup thesis (QPhoton + LSI) coherent with quantum-photonics roadmap.
scores.M_check: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form(form='8-K') confirms Feb 3 2026 8-K accession 0001213900-26-011452 (closing) and earlier Dec 15 2025 announcement; acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence (Mode B) on aggregate rollup.
scores.M_value: 8-K filings confirm the announce (Dec 2025) and close (Feb 3 2026). acq_coherence LLM tool returned INCOHERENT_ROLLUP / mean=0.0 but reasoning text said 'cannot assess... no target name provided' which contradicts the inputs sent. Tool appears to be giving a default low-input fallback rather than a real assessment.
scores.interpretation: Mode A confirms the acquisition is real (8-K filings, $110M cash). Mode B aggregate coherence call is unreliable due to apparent tool malfunction. Independent qualitative read: pairing a III-V laser-diode/photodetector fab (LSI/Freedom Photonics) with a TFLN PIC roadmap is plausibly synergistic — these are complementary photonics layers. However, the $110M cash spend (~7.5% of the 2025 equity raise) immediately after a $1.475B raise, on a Chapter 11 stalking-horse asset whose patents read mostly as laser/transmitter products (not quantum), is a thesis-broadening that softens the 'pure quantum' story. MOD: real deal, real assets, but the strategic logic is at the boundary of coherent extension vs. cash-deployment-driven scope creep. acq_coherence verdict treated as unreliable.

scores.claim_text: Raised $1,475.1M net via private placement, issuing 86.3M shares in 2025; insider behavior question (Mode B).
scores.M_check: sec_filings (S-1 list) (Mode A); insider_vs_calendar.query_insider_sales_near_budget_events(cik='0001758009', window_days=14, start_date='2024-01-01', end_date='2026-05-20') (Mode B).
scores.M_value: Mode A: 5 S-1 filings (Dec 2024, Jan 2025, Jul 2025 x2, Jul 2029) confirm registered resale shelf activity backing the $1.475B raise narrative — capital actually raised. Mode B insider_vs_calendar: n_form4_filings=20, total insider sales=19 transactions totaling $32,144,354. PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY signal — 1 discretionary sale (Begliarbekov Milan, $33,891, 2026-01-07, -13 days from FY26 bipartisan-budget signing). Tool clipped to lookback start 2025-05-20.
scores.interpretation: Mode A PASS on raise itself. Mode B: only 1 small ($34K) proximate discretionary sale to a budget event in the 12-month lookback, BUT total insider sales ~$32M against the company's $682K full-year 2025 revenue is itself a giant red flag — insider-cash extraction is ~47x the operating revenue. Per heuristic — the PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY flag plus the scale of total insider sales relative to operations qualifies this as SEVERE underdelivery. Capital was raised, but the dollar-weighted insider behavior (Form 4 cash-out >> operating revenue) is the kind of pattern the framework specifically targets.

scores.M_value: USAspending contracts: 2 awards totaling $95,663 ($69,500 DoC for TFLN chips + $26,163 NASA consulting). Grants: 0. Federal share of revenue therefore ~14% of total reported $682K revenue. No DoD contracts.
scores.interpretation: Revenue claim is true (and trivially small). The Mode A query confirms the federal share but exposes the SEVERE divergence between the company's positioning ('quantum computing for defense / govt grant pipeline') and reality ($96K obligated across 2 small awards over multiple years, ZERO DoD obligations under the QCi name). The company has a $1.5B war chest deployed against a sub-$1M operating business — classic capital-vehicle-with-no-business pattern. Material absence-where-presence-expected for the asserted defense/govt positioning.

scores.claim_text: Active securities class action (Feb 2025) + 4 derivative actions alleging false/misleading statements about customers, contracts, and business operations; class period 2020-03-30 to 2025-01-15.
scores.M_value: claim_evolution: 8 subsequent mentions across 10-K/10-Q/8-K/8-K/A, status REAFFIRMED_IN_STRUCTURED_DISCLOSURE, but no adverse findings flagged. 10-K/A history: 4 amendments — 3 prior amendments of the FY2022 10-K filed April/June/July 2023 and a Sept 2024 amendment. Multiple-amendment cycle on a single fiscal year's 10-K is a serious restatement footprint.
scores.interpretation: Three amendments of one fiscal year's 10-K (FY2022) plus an additional 10-K/A in 2024 demonstrate material disclosure-quality issues. Combined with an active securities class action specifically alleging false statements about customers/contracts/business operations, plus FOUR shareholder derivative suits, the pattern matches the framework's RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE template (governance + truthfulness-of-disclosure stress). Litigation is unresolved but the volume/repetition of amendments is itself a hard signal.

scores.claim_text: Plans to finance operations through U.S. government grant and loan programs (implied federal funding access).
scores.M_value: Federal presence: 1 UEI resolved (DMTDV6GZCQZ3), 2 contracts totaling $0.096M, 0 grants. Signal: SUB_MATERIAL_FEDERAL. DOE QIS programs are well-funded across FY25/FY26 (ASCR Advanced Computing Tech FY26 $112.6M, HEP-QIS FY25 $50.6M, BES-QIS FY26 $2.24B) — i.e., the funding exists; QCi is just not in it.
scores.interpretation: Mode B is load-bearing: DOE QIS funding is real and growing across primary lines, yet QCi has captured ~$96K total federal $$ vs. peers/competitors who get millions in SBIR-II and PE-line awards (compare to Freedom Photonics' own $25.8M DoD record under the same parent now). Disclosing 'U.S. government grant and loan programs' as a financing source is materially overstated when historical capture is sub-$100K and there is no current obligated pipeline. SEVERE underdelivery on implied federal-funding access.

scores.claim_text: Began commercializing Stevens Institute licensed technology but recorded zero royalty / zero related revenue.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Quantum Computing Inc', cutoff_date='2026-05-20') (Mode A); uspto_odp.query_assignee(assignee_name='Stevens Institute of Technology') (Mode B).
scores.M_value: edgar_fts: 474 hits across QCI filings (license referenced extensively). uspto_odp Stevens Institute: 285 applications, 69 granted patents broad — but the snippets shown are biomedical / ETF / actuators, not photonic-quantum-computing. Stevens Institute IP that underlies the License Agreement is held by Stevens but assignments to QCi would not show under QCi assignee.
scores.interpretation: The license is real and reaffirmed in 8 years of structured disclosure. However the claim is also a self-disclosed contradiction: 'begun commercialization' but $0 royalties + the broader 10-K shows $682K total revenue. The 3.5% Stevens royalty on net sales of licensed products implies effectively no commercial product sales at all of Stevens-IP-derived devices — modest claim survives because Mode A confirms agreement existence; modest gap because Mode B cannot find Stevens-Institute photonics-quantum patents that map clearly to the asserted commercialization. MOD.
